newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Amnesty concerned about proposed curbs in HK.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty concerned about proposed curbs in HK.

text.p: Amnesty International said on Friday it was concerned about plans by Hong Kong's future government to curb civil liberties after China takes over on July 1.
The London-based human rights group, which has close contact with other international bodies, would seek to exert pressure if human rights in Hong Kong deteriorated, a senior Amnesty official said.
"The proposed changes which we have seen ... recently I think raise cause for concern," executive director William Schulz said.

Schulz's comments came two days after Hong Kong's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa, launched plans to curb protests and foreign funding for Hong Kong political groups after the British colony years reverts to China at midnight on June 30.
Although widely expected, the plans have sparked a fiery debate locally and drawn criticism from the United States.
Schulz said his organisation, which has its main Asian centre in Hong Kong, would be able to draw on channels available to it should Hong Kong's human rights situation deteriorate.
The organisation worked closely with the United Nations and other inter-governmental organisations, and often met the press, and business communities, he said.
"We would attempt to raise these issues and assert influence through the appropriate channels available to us," he added.
